lines.text: A hundred years ago, a cobbler's boy walked out of Kamionka and became Fredi, Master of the Seventh Step.
The village still keeps his statue. It leans a little. So did he, after supper.
You mend boots in his village. At night, you practise his steps on the workshop floor.
Six steps you can count. The seventh, the songs say, nobody ever sees.
The Order takes no one without a Book of Duels: one hundred honest fights, each one witnessed and signed.
And there is only one place to find a hundred fights in a hurry.
So you sold the family goat and climbed onto Bartek's cart before you could change your mind.
Adi took bets on how soon you'd be back. Nothing personal.
In Brackwater, a one-eyed lanista called Magpie counted your goat money twice, then opened his ledger.
“Name,” he said. “Small letters. You haven't earned big ones yet.”
